entities.summary:
Zeno of Rhodes was a prominent ancient Greek politician and historian who played a crucial role in shaping the city-state of Rhodes during the Hellenistic period. Born on an unknown date, Zeno rose to prominence as a leader of the Rhodian faction that opposed the Macedonian Empire's expansion into the region.

In 197 BCE, he was appointed as one of the seven members of the Rhodian council, which governed the island. As a member of this council, Zeno worked tirelessly to promote the interests of Rhodes and its people, even going so far as to lead a diplomatic mission to Egypt in an attempt to secure Egyptian support for his city-state.

Despite his efforts, Zeno's time in power was cut short when he died in 200 BCE. However, his legacy lived on through his writings, which provided valuable insights into the politics and culture of the ancient Greek world.

One of Zeno's most famous works is his book 'The Chrepa', which chronicles the history of Rhodes from its founding to the present day. This work not only shed light on the city-state's development but also served as a testament to Zeno's own contributions to its growth and prosperity.

Zeno's impact on Rhodes was profound, and his legacy continued to shape the city's destiny for centuries to come.

The Chrepa, which translates to 'the unexamined life', serves as a fitting epitaph for Zeno's own life and work. His unwavering dedication to the people of Rhodes and his unrelenting pursuit of knowledge make him one of the most fascinating figures in ancient Greek history.
